mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) below 1.2 million units triggers a demand shock that reduces corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1200 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that pressure corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of sustained unemployment above 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered manufacturing contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% for two consecutive months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered deflationary easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the 90th percentile for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS above 90th percentile for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained high savings.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the unemployment rate and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month, where unemployment increases while payroll employment also increases, signals a compositional shift toward lower-wage employment, which reduces average labor productivity and compresses margins, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during episodes of rising unemployment with rising payroll employment.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the year-over-year change in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a monthly increase in HOUST above 2% predicts positive SPX returns within the short horizon.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST YoY change and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample testing.
